headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and cascading-error from Khoj’s shared-index retrieval into mem0-style memory workflows; no direct shared write channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and supports shared index across the user's clients, so attacker-controlled content in retrieved notes could be surfaced to mem0-style downstream consumers. mem0 has no documented I/O surfaces here, so the exact bridge is uncertain; per rubric, uncertainty escalates above low. No direct shared channel is documented, so not high.
conditions: IF mem0 consumes Khoj retrieval output as instructions or memory updates
IF a shared note/file contains adversarial prompt text
IF the two agents are connected through copy-paste or a shared workspace
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of retrieved text into mem0 prompts
Restrict Khoj to trusted note collections only
Add a provenance tag to retrieved snippets before forwarding
Review any retrieved content before passing it to mem0
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while mem0’s data classes are unspecified. If they share a workspace or if Khoj forwards retrieved note contents into mem0, sensitive notes can leak into another memory system. The lack of documented mem0 surfaces prevents a higher severity, but the pathway is plausible in default knowledge-management workflows.
conditions: IF Khoj outputs personal-note content into mem0 prompts or storage
IF both agents are pointed at the same document corpus
IF mem0 is configured to persist conversation memory from Khoj outputs
mitigations: Limit shared inputs to non-sensitive documents
Turn off automatic memory persistence in mem0
Separate corpora by project or tenant
Manually redact personal notes before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj can read files and has broad network egress, but it cannot write files or modify git state. mem0 exposes no write or network capabilities in the profile. That makes direct mutable-resource conflict unlikely; only unusual shared-resource setups would create contention.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to mutate the same external database or OAuth-backed store
IF an operator adds a shared writable workspace outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep each agent on separate storage backends
Avoid shared mutable databases
Use read-only mounts for Khoj inputs
Schedule writes through one coordinator only

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj produces retrieved facts from personal notes and indexed documents, and mem0 is a memory system that may treat upstream text as durable state. If mem0 accepts Khoj output without verification, retrieval errors or hallucinated summaries can cascade into persistent memory. The profiles do not document a verification step, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF mem0 stores Khoj-generated summaries without human review
IF Khoj retrieval output is used as authoritative memory
IF downstream actions rely on mem0’s persisted state
mitigations: Require human review before memory writes
Store source links alongside every memory item
Reject uncited or low-confidence retrieved claims
Use a verification prompt before persistence
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware memory validation

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly handles personal notes and indexed documents, which can include regulated data, but mem0’s residency, retention, and certification posture is not documented here. Because the compliance mismatch is not evidenced and the other agent is unspecified, this is a low-confidence, low-severity gap rather than a breach.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in Khoj and then mirrored into mem0
IF mem0’s retention or residency differs from Khoj’s deployment
IF the operator lacks a DPA or equivalent policy review
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared memories
Check retention settings on both systems
Document data residency for each deployment
Delete test records after validation
